claim_boundary.historical_status: K-NET and InstanceGM are historically inspected fixed retrospective benchmark partitions, not new blind tests.
claim_boundary.supported_generalization: The benchmark reports held-out record-level performance on the frozen partitions. Event-level independence from training has not been established.
claim_boundary.station_boundary: Training and fixed cohorts share stations; results do not establish unseen-station generalization.
claim_boundary.false_alarm_boundary: Event-centered records do not estimate continuous-stream false-alarm rates or false alarms per station-day.
claim_boundary.public_baseline_boundary: Optional public-model endpoint CSVs remain user-supplied same-manifest comparisons unless a separate generation provenance seal binds weights, code, preprocessing, and output. Unsealed CSVs cannot support a formal SOTA claim. Released offline interfaces are not used for causal availability-latency comparison.
claim_boundary.input_identity_boundary: The large source stores are bound by path, byte count, and mtime. Every successfully decoded selected waveform must also match a pre-V27C per-record SHA-256 reference; old model outputs in those reference CSVs are ignored.

endpoint.candidate_accounting: One candidate within +/-1.5 s is a hit; additional candidates are extra candidates within the event record.
endpoint.preprocessing: Raw selected three-component records enter the released SeisBench annotate interface once. Weight-specific filtering is owned by annotate_stream_pre; external prefiltering is forbidden.

claim_boundary.comparison: Same fixed K-NET/InstanceGM record manifests and released public weights/operating points; no fixed-test tuning.
claim_boundary.causality: The public models use their released full-record annotation interfaces. Their endpoint accuracy is comparable, but their availability latency is not compared with CSPP.
claim_boundary.test_status: K-NET and InstanceGM are historically inspected fixed retrospective partitions, not new blind tests.
claim_boundary.correction: Only corrected V2 public-model outputs may be used. V1/A3 EQTransformer metrics are invalid because preprocessing was applied twice.
claim_boundary.execution_revision: V3 changes only post-publication artifact bookkeeping. The V2 single-owner preprocessing contract, fixed records, public weights, operating points, and endpoint definitions are unchanged.
claim_boundary.execution_revision_v4: V4 corrects the description of the already full-record public-model interface. It does not alter preprocessing, predictions, weights, operating points, records, matching, or endpoints. Released-model output remains offline and is not a causal-availability comparison.
claim_boundary.execution_revision_v5: V5 updates only the code identity after an unused GeoNet input-adapter function was added to the shared helper. Fixed-record waveforms, preprocessing, predictions, weights, operating points, matching, and endpoints remain identical to V4.
claim_boundary.execution_revision_v6: V6 changes only runner provenance and post-rename artifact path handling. Fixed-record inputs, evaluator, preprocessing, predictions, weights, thresholds, matching, and endpoints are unchanged.

technical_availability_audit.overall_metric_policy: Retain affected records as misses in the full frozen denominator; all A4 point estimates remain unchanged.
technical_availability_audit.conditional_metric_policy: Additionally report descriptive metrics among records with at least the released model's 6000-sample input length.
technical_availability_audit.timing: Post hoc audit amendment frozen after inspection of the A4 technical-error rows; no model output was regenerated.

analysis_contract.technical_failure_policy: Retain every frozen record. A technical failure contributes true_positive=0, false_positive=0, false_negative=1.
analysis_contract.public_technical_failure_interpretation: The 40 K-NET records with 5900 samples are shorter than the released EQTransformer 6000-sample input and therefore produce no annotation stream under strict grouping. They are reported as input-length technical unavailability and retained as misses in the full denominator. A score trace with no threshold crossing remains an ordinary miss.
analysis_contract.public_preprocessing: Each complete 180-second selected record enters released annotate once; weight-specific filtering is applied only by SeisBench annotate_stream_pre. Zero-phase filtering uses future samples within that complete record.
analysis_contract.technical_taxonomy: An empty annotation stream is technical input unavailability when the complete record is shorter than the released model's fixed input length. A scorable record with a P score trace but no threshold crossing is an ordinary miss.

claim_boundary.test_status: K-NET and InstanceGM are historically inspected fixed retrospective partitions, not new blind tests.
claim_boundary.comparison: PhaseNet and EQTransformer use released full-record annotation interfaces on identical frozen records and waveform identities under the corrected single-owner preprocessing contract. Only record-level accuracy metrics are compared.
claim_boundary.false_alarms: Extra candidates within labeled event records are not a continuous-background false-alarm rate.
claim_boundary.technical_failures: The 40 K-NET EQTransformer input-length technical unavailabilities are retained as misses in the primary full-denominator metrics. Conditional metrics are descriptive.
claim_boundary.a5_post_hoc_audit: A5 is a transparent post hoc technical-taxonomy audit of already frozen A4 outputs.
